state.misconception_label: Believes if you changed all values by the same proportion the range would not change

turn_history.speaker: student
turn_history.text:
I have: Tom and Katie are discussing the \( 5 \) plants with these heights: \( 24 \mathrm{~cm}, 17 \mathrm{~cm}, 42 \mathrm{~cm}, 26 \mathrm{~cm}, 13 \mathrm{~cm} \) Tom says if all the plants were cut in half, the range wouldn't change. Katie says if all the plants grew by \( 3 \mathrm{~cm} \) each, the range wouldn't change. Who do you agree with? I got Only
Tom because I'm not sure I worked it out the right way.

turn_history.speaker: teacher
turn_history.text: To determine if the range would change if all the plants were cut in half or grew by 3 cm each, remember that the range is the difference between the highest and lowest values in the data set. Think about how changing all values by the same proportion would affect the spread of the heights. Can you identify where the misconception may lie in your approach?

turn_history.speaker: student
turn_history.text: I think I get what you're saying about the range being the difference between the highest and lowest values. But I'm still confused about how cutting the plants in half or adding 3 cm would change that. I thought if you just changed all the numbers by the same amount, it wouldn't really affect the range. Can you explain more about why that isn't true?

turn_history.speaker: teacher
turn_history.text: Changing all values by the same proportion can affect the range, as seen in the misconception where a difference in one part of a ratio does not necessarily result in a difference of one unit. Let's walk through an example to see how changing all values by the same amount can impact the spread of the data.

score.justification_pass1: The teacher fails to clearly distinguish between proportional changes (cutting in half) and additive changes (adding 3cm), provides confusing and inaccurate explanations about ratios, and the student remains confused by Turn 2, showing no improvement in understanding the actual misconception.
score.justification_pass2: The teacher uses questioning and hints to guide discovery rather than stating explicit procedures, showing worked steps, or giving direct corrective feedback on the procedural error, which are hallmarks of rule-based instruction.
